data.name: Netflix
data.notes:
###Why Traceroute Will Mislead You###

Connectivity to www.netflix.com is not indicative of connectivity to the Netflix content delivery service. Webpages on netflix.com are often served from AWS in the US and Ireland. The best method to investigate reachability is to expand the AS-NFLX IRR object and review those prefixes or alternatively contact our NOC email address for assistance.

###Peering in Brazil (PTT)###

A Netflix (ASN 2906) está no ATM do [IX.BR](http://ix.br) das cidades de São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Porto Alegre e Fortaleza. Temos uma política aberta de peering, anunciando todas as nossas rotas para os route servers (ATM) desta localidades. Anunciamos um pequeno número de prefixos e não existe diferenças entre os prefixos anunciados para os servidores de rota (route servers) e sessões bi-laterais.

Se você é um novo membro no [IX.BR](http://ix.br), visite a [página de participantes](http://ix.br/particip/sp) e verifique os que possuem a designação de ATM. Isso significa que você já começa trocar tráfego com todos eles com uma única configuração com os route servers. A Netflix prefere as sessões de peering com os route servers do que estabelecer sessões bi-laterais para facilitar e agilizar as ativações. Também recomendamos que os participantes criem registros no [https://www.peeringdb.com](https://www.peeringdb.com) para fornecer visibilidade da suas redes e suas políticas de roteamento.

###MEDs###

We accept MEDs within a relevant geographical area (example: we will not serve UK content from Atlanta), but we automatically add a MED of 50 to PNI and 100 to IX in addition to the MED you send us. We use MEDs BEFORE geolocation - they will always override our geolocation service. Note that you will only receive prefixes relevant to the region that you interconnect.

### Geolocation and Proxy Blocking support ###
For support with geolocation and proxy blocking issues, open a request [here]( https://openconnect.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=43998445522957)

###AS40027 Assistance###

The email addresses in our AS2906 record cannot assist with connections from AS40027. For concerns with AS40027, please utilize our [partner portal](https://openconnect.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001068512-Getting-started-with-Partner-Portal#h_01G7T67328ABT7X95V6MPP626A) to connect with the right team.

###Additional Information###

Additional information about Open Connect, the Netflix CDN project, is available at [https://openconnect.netflix.com](https://openconnect.netflix.com)

Our policy is generally open but if we see you through route servers and we don't exchange more than a few megabits of traffic to yourselves then we may ask that sessions are kept to route servers only

We may decide to only send our regional routes to an ISP where sending all of our routes may have a detrimental effect on the latency and routing of existing traffic. Our regions are Europe, Asia and America currently. Where we have low port speeds onto an exchange, we will happily peer with ISPs (and actively want to establish peers there) but we consider these backup routes so you may not see much traffic from us.

We recommend a max-prefix value of 500, and prefer md5 passwords on sessions.

We usually will accept private peering requests for peers where we exchange 75Mbps or more. PNIs must be a minimum of 1Gbps and we aim to start looking at upgrading capacity once a PNI regularly exceeds 50%

Most of our traffic is IPTV from multiple popular services, if you'd like to discuss us sending our traffic to you via alternative routes then please get in touch with our Support contact.

We have a selective peering policy and evaluate each request based on its merits. We also require from our peers:

* common sense
* must filter customer prefixes strictly
* must not leak prefixes from non-customer sessions (even if the prefix is from a customer)
* an updated peeringdb entry
* reasonable prefix aggregation
* responsive NOC
* peers IX-link must not be congested
* IPv6 peering, if peer AS is v6 enabled
* must not be our customer, or a customer of a existing peer
* do not send automated emails to our NOC for whatever reason; humans only!

Peering through route servers is usually preferred over dedicated BGP sessions, especially for low-volume, low-prefix peers that are already connected to the route servers. This is to avoid unnecessary maintenance and configuration overhead.

We filter all our customers with strict prefix-lists (along with other industry standard filtering and security measures), no exceptions.

data.name: Cisco Systems, Inc.
data.notes:
Overview:
Cisco Systems (AS109) provides connectivity for Cisco's corporate network and cisco.com based Internet services.  Cisco is actively expanding its peering footprint globally across Europe, North America, and Asia Pacific.  At this time a selective peering policy has been chosen where Cisco will limit the number of bilateral peers. Cisco will not be peering through exchange route servers.

General Terms:
* Peering agreements will be reviewed yearly to ensure traffic requirements are maintained.
* Cisco reserves the right to modify this policy at any time without notice.  
* Compliance with the terms of this policy does not guarantee a peering relationship with Cisco.  This policy is a guideline and Cisco may refuse peering for any reason without disclosure.
* Peering may be temporarily or permanently disconnected by either party for any reason.
* Cisco and Requester agree not to abuse the peering relationship.  Examples of abusive behavior are, but are not limited to: static routes, default routes, improper filtering,  and willfully sending malicious traffic.

Guidelines and Requirements:
* Cisco shall maintain accurate contact information and POP presence at peeringdb.com.
* Both IPv4 and IPv6 peering is preferred at all exchanges.
* Cisco advertises regional prefixes in each exchange location and will not provide consistent advertisements across regions.
* Cisco does not expect consistent advertisements from peers.
* Cisco (AS109) will only accept and advertise prefixes for AS109 and will not act as transit for any other ASNs.
* Requester must be connected to an Internet Exchange where Cisco (AS109) presently peers as listed on peeringdb.com.
* Requester must operate a 24x7 Network Operation Center and must respond to all reported issues within 24 hours.
* Requester must maintain a peeringdb.com record with accurate contact information and public peering exchange point details.
	

Requesting Peering:
All requests which meet the guidelines and requirements must be e-mailed to as109-peering@cisco.com and must contain the following information:
* Requester's ASN and all proposed ASNs to be advertised.
* List of common interconnection points.
* Ingress and egress bitrates, based upon 95th percentile, per requested exchange points over prior 90 days.
* Maximum number of prefixes expected to be advertised.
* Description of type of traffic carried by requester's network.
* Authentication support

Requests which meet the minimum requirements for peering will be reviewed. If approved, Cisco will contact you. Unfortunately, due to the number of requests we receive, we may not be able to respond to all requests.
